frequency_question: How often do structural frictions (such as legal challenges, operational friction from commercial bank tech readiness, or inter-institutional pushback) successfully block the implementation of such a announced or anticipated tool?
membership_rule: Includes any primary central bank action introducing an incremental or special reserve ratio on banking liabilities to absorb excess liquidity. Excludes standard statutory reserve ratio adjustments.

cases.name: PBoC Reserve Requirement Ratio targeted/incremental applications
Bank of Israel Special Levy / Reserve requirements experiments
Central Bank of Sri Lanka Statutory Reserve Ratio tier adjustments
National Bank of Poland additional reserve requirements trials

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named; represents distinct regulatory episodes across different jurisdictions.
known_gaps: Minor emerging market interventions that went unpublished or were aborted at an early internal stage before public friction could manifest.
skeleton: Total regulatory interventions of this specific class initiated by major central banks vs those abandoned prior to implementation due to structural or institutional pushback.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 documented attempts where authorities proceeded past draft stage.
validity_reason: Central bank legal powers and institutional autonomy over reserve mechanisms remain stable over multi-year horizons.
